newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end up, eye on Bakrieland.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end up, eye on Bakrieland.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended 1.05 percent higher on Friday in active buying in secondaries, with focus on property firm Bakrieland Development, brokers said.
A strong rebound in blue chip Telkom in late trading helped push up the index further, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index was up 7.42 points, or 1.05 percent, to 716.83 points.
On the week, the index had risen 4.6 points, or 0.65 percent. Gainers led losers by 85 to 55, with 58 counters unchanged on Friday. Total turnover was about 900 billion rupiah.
Noodle maker Indofood and cement maker Indocement of the Salim group were also actively sought, brokers said.

Sampoerna president-director Putera Sampoerna on Friday told a shareholders' meeting that the company was considering forming an alliance with Indonesia's largest conglomerate, the Salim Group, to boost Sampoerna's performance.
He currently has an about six-percent stake in Indofood and is a member of its board of commissioners.
Despite strong local buying this week, brokers and analysts expect the strength of the index to be limited on possible local-led profit-taking the coming week.
"Foreign buying is expected to be weak as Hongkong (market) will be closed until Wednesday for the handover. It might affect trading here," another broker with foreign firm said.
Brokers expect the index to range in the 711-720 point level.
